mcqs.learning_point: Identify examples of parallel lines in everyday objects
mcqs.question: Which of the following everyday objects contains a pair of lines that are parallel to each other?

options.A: Railway tracks on a train route
options.C: An open book with pages spread
options.D: A V‑shaped roof of a house

mcqs.answer: Railway tracks on a train route
mcqs.explanation: Railway tracks consist of two straight rails that run side by side and never meet, so they are parallel. Scissors intersect, an open book’s pages intersect at the spine, and a V‑shaped roof has lines that meet at the top, so they are not parallel.

mcqs.learning_point: Distinguish parallel lines from intersecting lines
mcqs.question: In a diagram, line l1 is drawn horizontally and line l2 slopes upward crossing l1. Which statement correctly distinguishes the two lines?

options.A: l1 and l2 are parallel because they are both straight.
options.B: l1 and l2 are intersecting because they meet at a point.
options.C: l1 and l2 are the same line.

mcqs.answer: l1 and l2 are intersecting because they meet at a point.
mcqs.explanation: Parallel lines never meet; intersecting lines cross each other at a point. Since l1 and l2 meet, they are intersecting. The other options describe incorrect relationships.

mcqs.question: Which pair of equations represents two parallel lines?
mcqs.explanation: Parallel lines have equal slopes. Both equations in option A have slope 2, so the lines are parallel. The other options have different slopes or are not linear equations.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand that parallel lines remain equally separated
mcqs.question: If the distance between two parallel lines is measured at two different points, what will the measurements show?
mcqs.explanation: By definition, parallel lines are equidistant at every point; therefore any two measurements of the separation will be equal. The other choices contradict this definition.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise parallel lines in geometric figures
mcqs.question: Which of the following geometric figures definitely contains a pair of parallel sides?
mcqs.explanation: In a square, opposite sides are parallel. A triangle has no parallel sides, a circle has no sides, and a regular pentagon’s sides are not parallel to each other.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify examples of parallel lines in everyday objects
mcqs.question: Select the everyday example that shows parallel lines.

options.A: Two rulers placed side by side on a desk
options.C: The arms of a clock at 3 o’clock
options.D: The edges of an open book

mcqs.answer: Two rulers placed side by side on a desk
mcqs.explanation: The two rulers are straight and never meet, so they are parallel. Crossing ladders intersect, clock hands intersect at the centre, and the pages of an open book intersect at the spine.

mcqs.learning_point: Distinguish parallel lines from intersecting lines
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes parallel lines from intersecting lines?

options.A: Two railway tracks are parallel; two roads that cross at a junction are intersecting.
options.B: Two roads that cross are parallel; two railway tracks intersect.
options.C: Parallel lines meet at a point; intersecting lines never meet.
options.D: Both parallel and intersecting lines are the same.

mcqs.answer: Two railway tracks are parallel; two roads that cross at a junction are intersecting.
mcqs.explanation: Railway tracks run side by side without meeting, making them parallel. Roads that cross meet at a point, so they are intersecting. Options B, C, and D describe incorrect relationships.

mcqs.question: A student draws two lines on graph paper. Line p has the equation y = 3x + 2 and line q has the equation y = 3x – 4. Which statement is true about these lines?

options.A: Lines p and q are parallel because they have the same slope.
options.B: Lines p and q intersect because their y‑intercepts are different.
options.C: Lines p and q are the same line.
options.D: Lines p and q are perpendicular.

mcqs.answer: Lines p and q are parallel because they have the same slope.
mcqs.explanation: Both equations have slope 3, so the lines are parallel. Different y‑intercepts only shift the lines vertically; they do not cause intersection. Perpendicular lines would have slopes that are negative reciprocals, which is not the case here.
